sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 10 (#9 agent_environment_and_network_posture_are_correct); Internal Quality Checks row 10 (#9, historical no-network wording, superseded by public-network note); Deterministic Checks rows 2, 15, 19, 23 (allowlist, offline constraint, literal secrets, manifest deps preinstalled)
evidence: Frozen task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24): build_timeout_sec=600.0, network_mode="public", cpus=2, memory_mb=4096; no docker_image, no allow_internet, no allowed_hosts anywhere in the task (grep empty). Lines 17-38 of task.toml are byte-identical to the frozen template's task.toml, and environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template Dockerfile (both sha256 0a75419e...d1). 2 CPU / 4 GB is sane for a node:22-bookworm-slim image with global express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (pinned) plus a single Express+SQLite app. No secret literals: [environment] has no env/secret keys; the only credential reference is the frozen [verifier.env] template ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""; a repo-wide grep for provider key shapes/PEM blocks in the task found nothing. Nothing secretly needs an install: solution package.json deps (better-sqlite3 12.4.1, express 5.1.0) exactly match the preinstalled pinned globals, server.js requires only those plus Node built-ins, solve.sh only copies files, and integration.md line 3 tells the agent the packages are preinstalled via NODE_PATH. raw-evidence-index entry 1 cites scripted golden runs in the agent image with the solve.sh-installed app (package.json/solve.sh/server.js hashes 242a3215.../f7c17a01.../e4d9402d... match current frozen bytes), consistent with the image being sufficient. Adversarial probes: an agent app adding extra npm deps can install them into /app/node_modules on the public network and Node resolves them from server.js's directory, so a conforming alternative is not penalised by the environment; a broken app cannot gain anything from this row's settings. Historical Internal sheet no-network wording is superseded by the current Quality Checks note that public is correct. I did not run a fresh Docker build; this row is satisfied by source/template evidence and is not a runtime-scoring claim.
